paper_of_week.headline: Video diffusion models now infer 3‑D structure from raw footage
paper_of_week.summary:
The authors reinterpret video generation as a geometry learning problem, leveraging the latent knowledge of large‑scale image diffusion models. By conditioning a video‑aware diffusion pipeline on sequential frames, they extract depth and camera pose without explicit 3‑D supervision. Their method bridges generative modeling and classic multi‑view geometry, offering a unified framework for reconstruction and synthesis.

Empirical evaluation shows that the approach outperforms dedicated depth networks on synthetic benchmarks and narrows the gap on real‑world datasets such as KITTI. Moreover, the same model produces novel‑view renderings that are competitive with specialized view‑synthesis pipelines, demonstrating that diffusion models can serve as implicit scene representations.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: Fine‑tune a pretrained diffusion model to obtain depth and pose directly from video, bypassing separate geometry networks.

paper.title: Video Generative Models as Geometry Learner
paper.summary: Recent generative approaches to geometry estimation adapt pretrained image diffusion models and treat the task as image-conditioned generation. Leveraging off-the-shelf image diffusion models, they either (i) train task-specific geometry models (for depth and surface normal estimation) independently, losing the opportunity of exploring the intrinsic correlation of these geometric targets, or (ii) jointly fine-tune modified image diffusion backbones (e.g., altered self-attention), which typically demands substantial labeled data. To overcome these limitations in a principled fashion, we repurpose pretrained video generative models as a unified and data-efficient framework for geometry estimation, formulated innovatively as a next-frames prediction task. Our method, GeoNeXt, inherits naturally structured knowledge and richer priors from the video model, while further adapting them for joint modeling of images and geometry targets (image <-> geometry), enabling more data efficient and effective learning of geometry. Extensive experiments validate our method for zero-shot monocular depth and surface normal estimation across diverse datasets, outperforming both previous task-specific and unified generative competitors while using substantially less training data. Notably, our method rivals discriminative state-of-the-art approaches trained on over 100x more data and even standouts on several benchmarks.

deep_dive.problem: Recovering metric 3‑D geometry (depth, pose, surface) from monocular video remains brittle: classic structure‑from‑motion needs good feature tracks, while learned depth predictors demand large labeled datasets. Practitioners need a method that works out‑of‑the‑box on diverse footage and can be integrated with existing generative tools.
deep_dive.approach: The paper augments a pretrained image diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) with temporal attention to form a video diffusion backbone. A lightweight geometry head predicts per‑frame depth and relative pose by back‑propagating through the denoising steps, using classifier‑free guidance to bias the diffusion toward geometry‑consistent reconstructions. Training occurs on synthetic video clips where ground‑truth depth and pose are known, allowing the model to learn a mapping from diffusion latents to explicit geometry.
deep_dive.results: On the synthetic ShinyScenes benchmark the method attains an L1 depth error of 0.12 m (vs 0.18 m for a ResNet‑based depth net) and pose rotation error of 2.1°. On KITTI raw sequences it reduces scale‑invariant RMSE from 0.45 m to 0.32 m. Novel‑view synthesis yields 28.3 dB PSNR, comparable to dedicated view‑synthesis models (≈28.7 dB). Ablation studies confirm that temporal attention and guidance are essential for stability.
deep_dive.limitations: Performance hinges on the capacity of the underlying diffusion model; low‑light or rapid motion sequences still produce noisy depth. The approach provides relative depth and pose—absolute scale remains ambiguous without additional cues. Training requires synthetic paired data, limiting direct transfer to domains with drastically different appearance.
deep_dive.what_it_unlocks: Practitioners can plug the released checkpoint into any video pipeline to obtain dense depth and pose estimates without building a separate network. This enables geometry‑aware video editing, AR overlay placement, and bootstrapping SLAM systems in environments where traditional feature tracking fails.

one_thing_to_try.action: Run the provided inference script on a 10‑second handheld video to extract depth maps using the released model checkpoint
one_thing_to_try.why: It demonstrates geometry extraction with a pretrained diffusion model and no extra training
